name: Cinnamon Roll Pancakes
desc: Pancakes with a piped cinnamon-butter swirl, steamed under a lid and finished with icing.

source.title: Cinnamon Roll Pancakes
source.evidence: Saved Instagram reel; caption and on-screen text captured in the owner's saved-recipes export

ingredients.raw: 2 to 3 tbsp unsalted butter, for the pan
1 tbsp water per batch, for steaming

steps: Batter: whisk the egg, milk and oil in a bowl. Add the flour, baking powder and sugar and whisk until just combined; a few lumps are fine.
Swirl: mix the softened butter, brown sugar and cinnamon, then stir in 1 tbsp of the batter so it holds together. Spoon into a piping bag or zip-top bag and snip a small corner.
Icing: whisk the powdered sugar with the milk, adding a few drops more if needed, until thick but drizzly.
Heat a large nonstick skillet with a lid over medium-low heat and add about 1/2 tbsp butter. Once the butter bubbles, add the batter in 1/4-cup scoops, leaving room between them.
When bubbles show on top, pipe a spiral of cinnamon swirl onto each pancake, starting in the center and stopping short of the edge.
Add 1 tbsp water to the pan (around the pancakes, not on them), cover and steam 4 to 5 minutes, until the tops are set and dry and the bottoms are golden brown.
Transfer to plates and repeat with more butter and the remaining batter. Drizzle with icing and serve warm.
tips: The butter in the pan crusts around the edges and makes them crunchy.
Watch the heat under the lid; the creator's first batch burned a little. Keep it at medium-low.
The creator only said "sugar" for the swirl; brown sugar is what most published versions use, and granulated works too.

references.title: Cinnamon Roll Pancakes
references.usedFor: medium-low heat, piping from the center outward and away from the edge, brown sugar in the swirl

references.title: Cinnamon Roll Pancakes with Cream Cheese Icing
